cards.q: Symptomatic bradycardia in an adult. First-line atropine dosing (AHA)?
options: 1 mg IV every 3–5 min, maximum 3 mg
0.3 mg IV once, repeated if needed
3 mg IV as a single bolus, then stop
cards.why: AHA: atropine 1 mg IV every 3–5 minutes up to 3 mg. Under 0.5 mg can slow the rate further.

cards.q: Transcutaneous pacing. How do you confirm mechanical capture?
options: A femoral pulse that matches the paced rate
A carotid pulse felt through the pacing jolts
A pacing spike on the monitor before each QRS
Twitching of the chest wall with each spike
cards.why: Pad current makes the neck muscles jump and can mimic a carotid pulse. Feel the femoral.

cards.q: Pacing captures at 60 mA. What output do you run?
options: Down to 40 mA to reduce pain
cards.why: A small safety margin above threshold stops beats dropping out without adding needless pain.

cards.q: K+ 7.4 with peaked T waves and a wide QRS. First drug?
cards.why: Calcium stabilises the myocardial membrane within minutes. Insulin–dextrose and salbutamol then shift potassium into cells.

cards.q: Stable regular narrow-complex tachycardia; vagal manoeuvres failed. Adenosine dosing (AHA)?
options: 1 mg/kg IV as a single bolus
cards.why: AHA: 6 mg rapid push then 12 mg. ERC continues to 18 mg for a third dose.

cards.q: Tachycardia with a pulse, BP 70/40 and chest pain. Treatment?
options: IV adenosine 6 mg, then reassess in 5 minutes
cards.why: An unstable tachyarrhythmia with a pulse gets synchronised cardioversion, with sedation if conscious.

cards.q: Adult shockable arrest. When is amiodarone 300 mg given?
cards.why: Amiodarone 300 mg IV/IO after the third shock; a further 150 mg after the fifth.

cards.q: Adult cardiac arrest. Adrenaline dose and interval?
options: 10 mg IV as a single dose
cards.why: 1 mg every 3–5 min: as soon as possible in non-shockable rhythms, after the third shock in shockable ones (ERC).

cards.source: AHA PALS 2020; ERC 2021 paediatric life support

cards.q: Adult proximal tibial IO. Where do you go in?
options: 2 cm medial to the tuberosity, on the flat tibia
Directly on the tibial tuberosity, perpendicular
Lateral to the tibial crest, on the fibular side
Just above the patella, into the quadriceps
cards.why: The flat anteromedial surface has thin cortex and marrow beneath; stay away from the joint and the tendon insertion.

cards.q: EZ-IO: tip resting on bone, before drilling. What tells you the needle is long enough?
options: A black 5 mm mark visible above the skin
The hub touching the skin before drilling
The needle is the blue (45 mm) set
It feels firm against the bone
cards.why: If no black line shows with the tip on bone, the needle may not reach the marrow: take a longer one.

cards.q: Awake adult with an IO in place. Before the pressure flush, give:
options: 2% preservative-free lidocaine 40 mg slowly through the IO
1% lidocaine with adrenaline through the IO
cards.why: Infusion into marrow hurts more than insertion. 40 mg over about 2 min, dwell, flush, then 20 mg.
